sources.title: Exact lesson cells and bounded CPU diagnostics
Byte offset is an injective disjoint ID map
sources.details: For each byte b∈{0,…,255}, f(b)=b+8 lies in {8,…,263}, disjoint from special IDs {0,…,7}; inverse on content IDs is g(i)=i−8. The map is one-to-one and concatenated UTF-8 bytes therefore recover the original valid UTF-8 text. 256+8=264. ASCII < is 60 and > is 62, so 68 and 70. <assistant> contains 11 ASCII characters, <image> contains 7. Control markers are excluded before decoding. This proves codec/structure separation, not a learned behavioral boundary.
